minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission spent most of the night on a public hearing about revising land use regulations, including firearm hunting on two town forests. It also continued several wetland hearings. A motion to approve the regulations failed and the vote was set for May 5.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted down a motion to approve its revised land use regulations as submitted, and set the vote again for May 5.
Most of the night was a public hearing on the regulations, including whether to allow limited firearm hunting on two town forests; the hearing was closed.
Residents spoke for and against firearm hunting near homes, and several said possession and hunting should be separate questions.
Hearings for 9 Bootwell Street, 137 Flynn Road and 757 Chase Road were continued to May 5; 48 Pearl Street, 101 Pleasant Street and 73 Peninsula Drive to May 19.
The 238 Fire Road 16 hearing was continued pending a revised plan removing wing walls and moving the limit of work to the 30 foot zone.

why_it_matters: The regulations decide whether firearm hunting is allowed on town conservation forests, so residents near those lands will see the question return on May 5.
Until the regulations are finished, the commission's trails grant for about 150 map signs cannot be put to use, as the chair described it.
watch_next: May 5 meeting: the second vote on the land use regulations, after the chair posts a revised version with the agent's new business form.
May 19 hearings for 48 Pearl Street, 101 Pleasant Street and 73 Peninsula Drive.
